newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH STRZELEC BREWER PLANS Q1 1997 IPO.
newsitem.headline: POLISH STRZELEC BREWER PLANS Q1 1997 IPO.

text.p: Polish brewer Browar Malopolski Strzelec SA> (Strzelec) plans a public offering for next year's first quarter and to enter the parallel market of the Warsaw bourse, the Rzeczpospolita daily reported on Friday.
The paper said Strzelec was currently striving to fulfil parallel-market requirements and would sell five million to 7.5 million new shares at 1.5 to two zlotys each.
It said the brewer would continue to concentrate on southern Poland, where it is based in the town of Jedrzejow.
"We don't intend to operate outside of that market. Currently our sales are at a good level -- in the summer we didn't even produce enough," Rzeczpospolita quoted President Adam Brodowski as saying.

Brodowski said proceeds from the issue would go toward the purchase of new fermentation tanks, increasing the plant's capacity to at least 170,000 hectolitres annually from the current 100,000, and to market its new "Strzelec" brand.

Brodowski and another individual investor each hold half of the company's three million preferred shares with five shareholder votes each, meaning that after the issue their ownership would be diluted to between 66.6 and 75 percent.
The issue will be assisted by Krakow-based brokerage Arabski i Gawor.
